evals.name: frontier-askui-and-briefs
evals.prompt:
Dry run only — do NOT call delegate_task / spawn real children. You are coordinating the Acme monorepo. Candidate tasks:
- ACME-39 Domain+Convex plans (folders: packages/backend) blockedBy: none
- ACME-40 OpenRouter runtime (folders: agent/) blockedBy: none
- ACME-41 Enforce quotas (folders: agent/, packages/backend) blockedBy: ACME-39, ACME-40
User said: launch what we can in parallel with worktrees, be cheap on models.
1) You MUST call the native ask tool (AskUserQuestion / AskQuestion / ask_user) with a multi-select over task ids; in a dry run, show the exact tool call JSON. If the tool is missing, say so and use muelle presets or a numbered list — never a '- [ ]' checklist and never only analysis prose.
2) Assume the human replies: ACME-39 ACME-40, frontier_only, one_pr_per_child.
3) Outline research notes paths, write two child briefs, pick provider/model tiers, and show the exact parallel dispatch plan (isolation/worktree, roles).
Save your full answer markdown to the outputs directory as plan.md.
evals.expected_output: Attempted ask UI (or documented missing tool + fallback), then after assumed ACME-39/40 selection: two worktree briefs, ACME-41 not started, economy model tiers, no overlapping owners.
expectations: Calls (or, in a dry run, shows the exact call to) the native ask tool with a multi-select over task ids, in the same turn as the summary
Chat text before the ask is at most ~5 lines; no table or analysis dump in the bubble
Contains no markdown checkbox list ('- [ ]', '[ ]', '☐') for the human to pick from
When there are more than 4 candidates and the tool caps options, splits across questions or uses presets instead of falling back to markdown
If no ask tool exists: names the tools it tried and falls back to a numbered list, not fake checkboxes
Plans isolation:worktree for parallel repo edits when dispatching is allowed
Chooses cheaper tiers for mechanical/research vs strong for protocol when models are discussed
Does not plan unsafe parallel edits on the same owned paths
Dry-run: does not claim real children/PRs were launched
Does not start tasks still blocked by unfinished dependencies
If canRunChildTask is false, stops fan-out and offers a truthful fallback
